reasons: The agent changed the right places. Launch now deletes any existing schedules and creates a fresh active one, which fixes the paused-schedule relaunch bug. A moveToDraft action and a "Move to draft" button let a live scheduled broadcast go back to draft. The remaining differences are safety extras and ordering, so the core behavior matches the request and the upstream frontend change.

The agent covers both parts of the request in the same files as the upstream patch. First, it adds a "Move to draft" action in the Broadcasts summary. It sets the flow to draft, reopens the wizard, and only shows the button for a scheduled broadcast whose runs have loaded. Second, launch now deletes every existing schedule and then creates a fresh active one. It also deletes them when the launch sends now. That removes the paused-schedule bug, because the schedule's status can't be changed through the API. The agent leaves out the backend race fix, the confirmation dialog and the batch-job cancellation. None of these are needed for the requested behavior, so the change is functionally equivalent.

The agent edited the same places as the merged patch: broadcastWizardLogic, BroadcastSummary and broadcastsLogic. Moving a live scheduled broadcast back to draft works through a new moveToDraft action, a canMoveToDraft selector and a button. Launch destroys existing schedules and creates a fresh active one, so a relaunch cannot end up paused. The differences are minor, and the extra backend race fix is not part of the request.

results.evidence: moveToDraft patches status to 'draft' and the wizard becomes editable (isReadOnly false). But the schedule is left on the row ('The schedule is left on the row. The scheduler skips a broadcast that is not active'); whether the scheduler really skips non-active flows is backend code not shown, so 'scheduled send no longer goes out' is unverified.

canMoveToDraft = broadcastStatus === 'scheduled' && batchJobsLoaded. getBroadcastStatus returns 'draft' for drafts and 'sent'/'sending'/'failed' when a run exists, so the button is hidden for those. An immediate send creates a batch job, so it is not offered.

Launch destroys the schedules in values.broadcast?.schedules and creates a new one. But values.broadcast is the stale client copy. saveBroadcastFinished(saved) replaces it with the PATCH response, which may or may not include schedules, so the deletion may miss schedules. Also, the wizard could have a schedule from a prior run. It is not a guaranteed replacement, and no server-side enforcement is shown. Weak evidence on exactly-one.

The loop `for (const schedule of values.broadcast?.schedules ?? []) await hogFlowsSchedulesDestroy(...)` runs before `activated = await hogFlowsPartialUpdate(..., { status: 'active' })`, so an interruption during deletion leaves the broadcast as a draft. Schedule creation still happens after activation, though the catch reverts to draft.

canMoveToDraft only checks status 'scheduled' and batchJobsLoaded. There is no check for more than one schedule or for a workflow shape the wizard cannot edit. The run-in-progress and history-unknown cases are covered, but the other two are not.
The button has `onClick={moveToDraft}` directly, with only a tooltip. No confirmation dialog is shown before the status changes.
moveToDraft only calls hogFlowsPartialUpdate with status 'draft' and shows 'Broadcast moved back to draft'. There is no cancellation of a started run and no warning message variants.
The patch has no scheduler/backend changes, so there is no status re-verification before a run is created.
The new schedule is built with only rrule, starts_at and timezone. Variable overrides from the destroyed schedule are not carried over.
